drills.q: Implement Union-Find with path compression and union by rank.
drills.a: find recursively repoints every visited node to the root; union finds both roots, attaches the shorter-rank tree under the taller, and increments rank only when ranks are equal.

drills.q: Count the number of connected components (provinces) given an adjacency matrix.
drills.a: Union every pair with a matrix entry of 1; maintain a running count initialized to n, decremented on every successful (non-redundant) union.

drills.q: Given a list of edges forming a graph that was originally a tree plus one extra edge, find the redundant edge.
drills.a: Process edges in order, calling union on each; the first edge whose union call returns false (both endpoints already share a root) is the redundant edge.

drills.q: Given == and != equality constraints between variables, determine if they can all be satisfied simultaneously.
drills.a: Union all == pairs first. Then check every != pair does not share a root; if any != pair ends up connected, the constraints are unsatisfiable.

drills.q: Explain precisely what amortized complexity union-find achieves with both optimizations, and what happens with only one.
drills.a: Both together: O(alpha(n)) amortized (Tarjan 1975). Union by rank alone: O(log n) worst case per find. Path compression alone (arbitrary union order): O(log n) amortized. Neither: adversarial order can force O(n) per find.

drills.q: Extend union-find to answer ratio queries between variables given equations like a/b=2.0 (Evaluate Division).
drills.a: Store a weight alongside each parent pointer representing the ratio to that parent; during find, accumulate (multiply) weights along the compressed path so each node holds a direct ratio to the root; union combines two components using the equation linking them.
